timingAndReporterLimitations.scope: All twelve completed managed jobs; raw API job times and retained JSON artifacts, data only.
conclusions: All hits reuse only the reviewed 47-test file; 119 native project/file instances still execute.
The native release-test tail remains required on c2 through c11.
Removing measured work in arithmetic does not establish an implementable or measured future speedup.
The managed reporter preserves full test names and states, but its nested suite counts, ancestor/title structure and timing metadata are incomplete.

fullJobGapReview.reviewMode: read-only source inspection and trusted JSON-only artifact component analysis; no source edits, runtime tests, builds or dispatches
fullJobGapReview.observedWindowStatus: still running at review; this is not a full-window result

componentAudit.scope: authenticated artifact components and same-commit c0/control plus c1 origin-authorized replay only; coordinator log/API and final full-window checks remain pending

steps.name: retain managed execution and merged full-suite evidence

observedC1.arithmeticOnly: Subtracting the recorded test step of 17 seconds from 37 yields 20 seconds, 3 above 17. This frozen-step subtraction is not a future performance forecast.

merelyImplementationMissing.detail: One-candidate dispatcher and47-count expectation must become a finite selected(project,file) roster with one authenticated closed identity per instance; repeated Zod paths cannot collapse.

A reviewed adapter can in principle key and apply aliases, inline dependency resolution, expectedZodAlias context and version-specific selected-file sets without granting filesystem/network to tests. No execution proof exists yet.

Current hit imports native Vitest and recompiles modules after dependencies exist. A finite reviewed preparation/closure plan could verify source/config/discovery/negative lookups before those imports; arbitrary dynamic config cannot be trusted from a cached manifest.

declaredContractBlockers.detail: Actual tests create Request/Response/Blob and storage operations that are explicitly guarded today. Coverage needs a separately keyed deterministic facade/profile with completion accounting; unguarding native objects does not preserve the current evidence claim.

jsdom, React transforms, DOM state/events and hoisted module mocking are absent from this runtime. Preserving intended UI test behavior requires a reviewed compatible environment/compiler or a separate managed native environment; changing environment=edge-runtime would change the tests.

The actual npm release test uses node:test, filesystem writes, generated executables, subprocess trees, Git repositories and loopback HTTP. Native modules are rejected by compiler and no such capabilities are exposed. It cannot run unchanged in the existing closed workerd contract.

feasibility.existingNativeUnitsAreNotAProvenSubstitu: Managed mode disables that binary, existing corrected observers decline relevant metadata, and its stated proof assumes nonadversarial programs. No earlier receipts or ignored observations supply a managed full-job authority.

boundedNextImplementation.requirement: Record exact original command chain and selected 120 (project,file) instances, per-instance aliases/context/config/source/closure identities and release-script/workflow closure. A full hit requires authenticated successful evidence for every selected instance and every conditional tail; otherwise it must execute the missing or declined work. Newly added tests or changed discovery must invalidate the relevant plan.

Add reviewed keyed alias/context preparation for pure Zod/edge units. For jsdom and release integration, first build a separate finite managed Node/OS profile with pinned Node/npm/Git/toolchain, explicit environment, closed readonly inputs and private writable scratch, isolated owned loopback/subprocess tree, and enforced treatment of clock/random/native I/O. Preserve actual React, Node, npm and Git semantics exercised by these tests. This boundary work is not supplied by repeated successful outputs or by an allowlist edit.

boundedNextImplementation.component: Whole-command receipt and faithful report/effect composition
boundedNextImplementation.requirement: Compose complete per-instance/report and release-tail evidence with original command exit/console/output files. A full replay starts no Vitest or node:test worker only after all child authorities and command conditions match; any observed failure remains failure. Retain nested suite metadata and project multiplicity rather than claiming full native JSON fidelity from the current assertion-only formatter.

boundedNextImplementation.component: Early Action plan for dependencies and build outputs
boundedNextImplementation.requirement: Decide complete install/build/test hits before restoring dependencies or bootstrapping Vite/esbuild when their use is unnecessary. Restore separately authenticated required build outputs and preserve install lifecycle/input identity; a passing test receipt does not authorize skipping npm ci or the TypeScript/esbuild build. Intercept the unchanged npm command chain through a reviewed plan even when Vitest is not installed, and keep miss behavior native.

Retain setup, Action/cache latency, validation/upload and post steps in actual job duration. Use real new cold control/window results after the new contracts pass their failure/authority/discovery matrices; no current speed or floor+8 guarantee follows from this design.

stillNecessaryUnderFrozenProfile: Native119 Vitest instances preserve unsupported environments, aliases/context and HTTP/storage behavior.
The original npm release tail still executes outside the managed Vitest bridge from c2 onward.
Native preparation, closed bundle compilation and capability preflight are part of current receipt validation before lookup.
Dependency restoration/install misses and real build outputs have no complete-job managed authority.
Artifact comparison/upload and cleanup are part of the measured job; their cost cannot be removed from accounting.
forbiddenShortcuts: Do not label the47-test receipt hit as a full-job hit.
Do not omit119native instances, release counters, build outputs or changed-file discovery to meet the budget.
Do not use a cached local manifest as receipt authority or accept old-policy receipts.
Do not unguard native capabilities, ignore descriptor metadata or rely on agreeing repeated outcomes as a closed input proof.

references.finding: Only one explicit candidate is supported; default candidate count is47.
Each candidate decision currently prepares native Vitest, compiles preflight/test and keys actual policy+host before lookup.
All other native project/file instances execute through ordinary-remainder, then their complete report rows are merged.
Admission requires convex-helpers project, edge-runtime, no setup/global setup/provided context/snapshot/coverage; this is an explicit finite policy.
Actual specification discovery imports installed Vitest and executes reviewed configuration on every decision.
Compiler uses browser bundling and default package resolution, without a Vite project alias adapter.
Native modules are rejected except the reviewed async-local-storage facade/private implementation.
Managed TestRunner has providedContext {}, declared managed SSR environment, denied unexpected RPC, one static test entry.
Only explicit environment/nextTick is exposed as process; allowed globals exclude DOM and Request/Response/Blob.
All unlisted ambient globals and fetch/crypto are guarded; native HTTP/storage host objects must not simply be unguarded.
Zod projects require version-specific aliases, expectedZodAlias context and inline zod-compare dependency resolution.
Actual tests read expectedZodAlias via Vitest inject().
UI project selects jsdom and React Vite plugin, not edge-runtime.
UI test uses hoisted vi.mock/vi.importActual and a real document reset.
UI test renders React via testing-library and accesses document.
Remaining edge test creates and exercises Request/Response headers locally.
Remaining edge test stores Blob values in Convex test storage.
Remaining edge test uses Blob-backed storage.
Build emits TypeScript/esbuild outputs; npm test is Vitest followed by node --test release scripts at c11.
Release test directly imports filesystem, child_process, process, os and node:test.
Release fixture creates/copies writable scratch repositories, symlinks installed dependencies and executes generated npm/editor wrappers.
Release fixture inherits real environment, invokes Node/npm/git, initializes repositories and pushes to a private bare Git remote.
Release tag test binds a loopback HTTP server and spawns actual Node to exercise workflow code against it.
Generic Node --test commands are not managed interceptions.
Managed interception delegates only repository-root Vitest invocation.
Managed Action deliberately writes quod:null; the legacy native unit recorder is not enabled by this profile.
Native unit hook is separate, and scripts containing Vitest are deliberately excluded from that unit path.
Native unit path requires a separate Quod binary and skips a script closure containing Vitest.
Npm dependency tree restore currently precedes the install hit.
Action waits for dependency restore, task cache setup and Vitest setup before reporting ready.
Window keeps install/build/test commands; managed Action enables no task cache or Cloud and does not cover outer release tail.
Independent comparison, upload and Action post cleanup remain inside full runner duration.
Legacy native unit proof uses a syscall trace plus two witnesses and explicitly assumes nonadversarial test/build code; it is not the managed closed-realm contract.
Existing native observer fails closed on descriptor metadata without a stable pathname or on unlinked descriptors.
Earlier verified window found build and test:release declined on descriptor metadata; ignoring this is not a safe reuse fix.
